newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Mao corrects accent 20 years after death.
newsitem.headline: China's Mao corrects accent 20 years after death.

text.p: Two decades after his death in 1976, Mao Zedong has finally abandoned his thick local dialect for the measured tones of standard Mandarin Chinese.

Filmmakers shooting a series of movies on Mao had switched the voices used on dubbing soundtracks to give the late Great Helmsman a Mandarin accent that he never had in real life, the China Youth Daily said on Wednesday.

All producers should do their best to get used to the new accents and to help audiences accept the new speaking style of Mao and other former leaders portrayed in the linguistically correct movies, the newspaper quoted officials as saying.
"Language should not be an obstacle in the way of people's appreciation of the beautiful," the newspaper said.

Standard Mandarin, known as "common speech", is China's official language, but many of the nation's people and leaders are more comfortable speaking local dialects which are often mutually unintelligible.
Mao himself delighted in his rural roots in southern China's Hunan province and spoke with a thick Hunanese accent.
